//: Copy to capture.local.json, which is gitignored. Environment variables of the same name win. Run `dotnet run --project tools/StubId.CaptureHarness -- check --broker=neb` to see what is missing and which steps it costs.
//published: The broker publishes credentials for its open test clients in its integration documentation, so anyone can exercise pre-production. Needed for the front-channel step.
STUBID_NEB_PP_CODE_CLIENT_SECRET: the published open code-flow client secret
//private: A client of your own, if you have one. It carries the richer scopes: ssn, nemid.pid, ssn.details_*, userinfo_token and transaction_token.
//sso: Two clients joined to the same service provider's single sign-on, which is a switch on the Advanced tab of the broker's client administration. Both need it Active, or the second one prompts and the recording shows nothing. Otherwise: grant type Code, PKCE Active, Userinfo Token Active, and 'accept all redirects' OFF with only http://localhost:5099/callback registered - which also makes client A serve as the unregistered-redirect case.
//hybrid: Same again but with grant type Hybrid, which is the only way to observe c_hash. ASP.NET Core requires it whenever an id_token arrives through the front channel.
//signicat: The second broker's sandbox, whose tenant is its hostname. That is the difference worth knowing before you record anything: the first broker's pre-production host is public and shared, so no recording of it could say whose it was, while your Signicat subdomain sits in the issuer, in every absolute URL inside the discovery document, and in iss in every token. Register it before the first recording rather than after one.
//signicat-scan: These four are also what the committed-file guard searches the working tree for, and it can only look for what is set here. A value left blank is replaced in nothing and searched for nowhere, which looks exactly like a value that was never needed - run `dotnet run --project tools/StubId.CaptureHarness -- check --broker=signicat` to see which of them it can look for.
STUBID_SIGNICAT_DOMAIN: the subdomain your sandbox answers on, without .sandbox.signicat.com
//signicat-key: The key identifier of the signing key registered on the client, which is what a signed request object names in its header. Not a secret, and not the broker's either - it names a key on your client.

redact.//: Values that must not reach a fixture, as replacement-to-original. A personal number is replaced by the same number with 60 added to the day (01-09 to 61-69, 10-19 to 70-79, 20-29 to 80-89, 30-31 to 90-91), which cannot be anyone's and keeps the length and shape a fixture depends on. The example below uses the 31st of February, which nobody was born on, so it shows the mapping without printing a number that might be someone's. Register both the bare and the separated form: the scrubber matches exact strings. A transaction token names the receiving organization, so its name and CVR belong here before recording one, as does the test identity's name.
redact.//blanked: Two claims are blanked by name and need no entry here: transaction_client_ip and mitid.geo_ip_distance_km, both of which describe the client rather than the broker. Neither value can be known in advance - one is handed out by a router, the other computed per sitting - so a rule keyed on the value would be right once. StubID reproduces neither, so nothing is lost. A test also fails on any routable address anywhere in the repository, and the client identifiers above resolve from the settings themselves.
redact.Synthetic Testperson: the identity's name as MitID returns it
